display: I run Fio, a small knitwear label in Lisbon where every collection is built around one hand-made detail I can trace to a named person.

signals.text: I'm looking for experienced hand embroiderers for a twelve-piece knitwear capsule, at least 80 small panels.
My embroidery budget is around 25 euros per panel, and the quotes I've had are 90 to 140. I'm looking for a different way to do this, not just a cheaper quote.
The embroidery panels are about 18 by 12 cm and go on sleeves and hems. The sampling deadline is the end of November, and a stockist in Antwerp wants the embroidery in a deeper green.
I phoned embroidery ateliers in Porto and Lyon. Porto only does bridal and church linen, and Lyon wanted a thousand-euro setup fee. I don't have a proper list of who does this kind of work.
I have a small creative-industries grant that has to be spent by December. I've been avoiding the paperwork and could use someone who has done this before.
I need final AW samples ready for a stockist order deadline on 15 December.
My studio flatmate leaves for Berlin on 1 November. I have to decide whether to keep the whole Marvila studio or move to a desk in a shared atelier near Anjos.
Working from home isn't an option because my flat is nine square metres. I'm looking for workable studio or desk space.
I keep looking at the numbers hoping they change. I'm tired and lose sleep over the budget.
I think about whether a label that makes fewer pieces at higher prices can last. I'd like to talk to other small makers who have worked this out.
I'm learning to surf in Ericeira and enjoy it a lot. I'd happily meet other beginners.
I'm planning to use a mustard merino from my yarn archive for a coat collar, and I'm looking for a good hand-made button or trim to go with it.

offers.text: I can design and produce small-batch knitwear, about 400 pieces a year, on two industrial knitting machines (a Stoll and a Shima Seiki) plus a hand-flat machine for samples.
I have a sample room with six years of pattern archives and fit blocks, and I can do pattern fittings with a model.
I know a wool spinner in Covilhã and a hand-dyer in Guimarães, and I can introduce them to makers who need yarn or colour work.
I sell through eight European stockists, including shops in Copenhagen, Antwerp and Porto. I can show other makers how I approach shops.
I have a newsletter with about 1,800 subscribers and a 41% open rate. Its readers like stories about the people who make the pieces, so I can feature a collaborator's work in it.
I know how to trace and document a hand-made detail back to a named maker, such as a family in Viseu who make buttons, and I can share how I do it.
I can offer paid, credited work on a capsule to a maker whose hand skills fit it. I can't pay at atelier rates, but I can give the maker visibility, a named credit and repeat work.
I can host small knitwear sampling sessions in my Marvila studio.

catchers.hypo: Hi, I embroider by hand in a small village. I've made linen and wool pieces for years but never for a fashion label. Would you want to try sleeve panels?
catchers.can: I can send a paid sample brief with the panel size (18 by 12 cm), thread colours and deadline, and credit the embroiderer by name on the piece.
catchers.confirm: Do you embroider by hand yourself, or manage a team that does, and can you make panels of about 18 by 12 cm?

catchers.hypo: I teach embroidery to a group of older women in the Alentejo. Several of them would like paid work with clear design briefs.
catchers.can: I can ask my grandmother in Elvas whether anyone nearby still does hand embroidery, and I can offer a named, credited brief to a small group.
catchers.confirm: Are your embroiderers in the Alentejo, Portugal, and willing to work from a design brief for a label?

catchers.hypo: I'm a textile student with a good hand-embroidery portfolio and I need real production experience. I can work for a lower rate if it goes in my portfolio.
catchers.can: I can offer a small paid commission, a credit and a reference, and a way into a real production run with a European stockist.
catchers.confirm: Can you produce at least ten embroidered panels of a consistent standard before the end of November?

catchers.hypo: I'm a knitwear technician moving to Berlin and I'm looking for freelance machine-knitting work or a studio contact.
catchers.can: I can introduce my studio flatmate Rui, a knitwear technician who is moving to Berlin on 1 November, or tell you what I know about technician work on Stoll and Shima Seiki machines.
catchers.confirm: Do you work with industrial flat-bed knitting machines, such as Stoll or Shima Seiki?

catchers.hypo: I run a small shared atelier near Anjos with a few free desks. Do you need a place to work?
catchers.can: I can consider taking a desk and tell you how much space and storage I'd need for sample work and machine access.
catchers.confirm: Is the desk in Lisbon, with space for storing yarn and samples?

catchers.hypo: I've applied for creative-industries grants in Portugal before. Would you like help structuring the spending report?
catchers.can: I could swap grant-paperwork help for samples, a pattern session or a feature in my newsletter.
catchers.confirm: Have you completed a Portuguese creative-industries grant report before?

catchers.hypo: I make buttons, trims or hand-dyed yarn in small batches and I'm looking for knitwear labels that care where things are made.
catchers.can: I can look at your work for my coats and sleeves and credit you by name. I can also introduce my existing yarn and dye contacts.
catchers.confirm: Do you make the items yourself, or do you resell items made elsewhere?

catchers.hypo: I'm a beginner surfer in Lisbon and I'd like a partner for lessons at Ericeira on weekends.
catchers.can: I can share what I learned from my first lessons, including where to rent a wetsuit, and bring my friend Marta if she is free.
catchers.confirm: Are you a beginner who can get to Ericeira on a weekend morning?

forbids.text: I only use hand-made details that I can trace to a named maker, so I won't use anonymous outsourced embroidery or mass-produced decoration.
I can't afford a full-time assistant, so I can only offer project or per-piece work.
I can't pay standard atelier rates of 90 to 140 euros per panel, and I won't pay big setup fees.
I won't commit to a collaborator before I've seen a sample.
I don't share anything about my finances beyond the project budget, nor details about my family.

projects.name: Capsule AW27 'Margem'
projects.text: A twelve-piece knitwear capsule with hand-embroidered sleeve and hem panels (about 18 by 12 cm, at least 80 of them). The sketches and knit base are done. The embroidery is the open problem, with a sampling deadline of 30 November and a stockist order deadline of 15 December.

projects.name: Studio move
projects.text: My studio flatmate is leaving on 1 November. I'm deciding between keeping the Marvila space and a desk in a shared atelier near Anjos.
roles_needed: studio-mate for knitwear or textile work

policy.t1: When there's a real lead, I'll share details of the Margem capsule: the embroidery I need, panel size, rough per-panel budget, and the deadlines.
policy.t2: Once the match looks strong and I know who the other person is, I'll talk about the studio costs and how the label is really doing.
policy.never: Loan details, family finances, and personal worries about family or my own health.
